summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The five calls are neutral with low conviction: Amgen and Gilead are still stretched, Microsoft lost its trend check, and Monster is a first call. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: This week the brain looks at five runners. Two are out of breath from sprinting, one has slowed down, and one new runner joined the watch list. Picking runners did no better than luck before, so the brain only watches with pretend money. The family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. This is the week's buy: the same amount as always goes into the whole-market fund for money we will leave alone for years, and money we may need soon stays safe. The market's trend leans down; steady buying through a slow patch is exactly the plan.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. Last week's bet finished ahead, so the weekly game should stand at two weeks won and one lost once it is scored. A coin does that often enough that it proves nothing yet. This week we place a fresh bet.

Third, a lesson. A month ago Microsoft looked like one of our strongest names; now it has lost its trend. Strength that looks permanent rarely is, which is why we own the whole market instead of guessing which leader lasts.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
